units.source_text: 我问K搬到新居后的心情如何时，他只说了句“不坏”。

en.t: When I asked K how he felt after moving into his new place, he only said, "Not bad."

units.source_text: 让我说的话，就不只是“不坏”了。

en.t: If you ask me, it was far more than merely "not bad."

units.source_text: 以前他住的是阴湿、肮脏的北屋，饭食也同那房子一样难以下咽。

en.t: Before that he had lived in a damp, filthy north-facing room, and the food was as hard to swallow as the room itself.

units.source_text: 他搬到我这里来，真可谓是出自幽谷，迁于乔木。

en.t: His move to my house was truly like coming out of a dark valley and moving up into a tall tree.

units.source_text: 他之所以没有露出欣喜的神色，一是由于他性格倔强，二是由于他一贯的主张。

en.t: The reason he showed no sign of delight was partly his stubborn nature and partly the principles he always held.

units.source_text: 他是在佛教教义的熏陶中成长起来的人，认为衣食住行上的铺张是非常不道德的。

en.t: He had been raised under the influence of Buddhist teachings and regarded extravagance in food, clothing, and shelter as deeply immoral.

units.source_text: 他只言片语地读过一些古代高僧、圣哲之类的传记，养成了动不动就想将精神与肉体分离开的习性。

en.t: Having read bits and pieces of biographies of ancient eminent monks and sages, he had acquired a habit of trying to separate spirit from flesh at every turn.

units.source_text: 说不定，他甚至觉得鞭挞肉体能够增加灵魂的光辉。

en.t: He may even have felt that scourging the body could increase the radiance of the soul.

units.source_text: 我尽量凡事都顺从他，因为我在致力于把冰拿到向阳处融化。

en.t: I tried to yield to him in everything as much as possible, because I was trying to bring the ice into the sunlight and melt it.

units.source_text: 我相信，如果不久冰融化成了温暖的水，K自我觉醒的时机就会到来。

en.t: I believed that once the ice soon melted into warm water, the moment would come for K to awaken to himself.

units.source_text: 1.出自幽谷，迁于乔木：出自《诗经·小雅·伐木》：“伐木丁丁，鸟鸣嘤嘤。

en.t: 1. "Coming out of the dark valley and moving into a tall tree" comes from the Book of Songs, Xiaoya, "Felling Trees": "The trees are felled with ringing strokes; the birds call in harmony."
It continues: "They come out of the dark valley and move into the tall trees."

units.source_text: 原指鸟儿从幽深的山谷迁移到高树上去，比喻乔迁新居。

en.t: Originally it referred to birds moving from a deep valley up into high trees, and it became a metaphor for moving into a new home.

units.source_text: 此处借喻由低处往高处走。

en.t: Here it is used figuratively to mean going from a low place to a higher one.
